thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: EU-west canary health spike after green swap — elevated 5xxs and latency, partial traffic still hitting old pool due to DNS TTL sticky behavior.

alice_oncall: paging ben for on-call handoff. seeing ~12% 5xxs from eu-west for model endpoints. customers reporting timeouts.

ben_sre: on it. joining call. can you paste the canary rollout command?

carol_prod: deploy-bot posted rollout at 14:12UTC: `swapper --region eu-west --green weight=60% --canary=true --ttl=120s`

ben_sre: looking at route53 metrics — most clients respect TTL but some edge caches stuck on old A records. weight flip succeeded in control plane but DNS sticky clients still routing to old green pool causing backend mismatch.

alice_oncall: impact: some customers seeing 502/504, higher token latency. support tickets rising. marking sev2 for now.

deploy-bot: Rolling back canary to last stable: `swapper --region eu-west --set weight=0% --target blue` (in progress)

ben_sre: quick check: `curl -v https://eu-west.api.redwood.ai/health` -> intermittent 502 from 3/10 edge IPs. attaching sample trace:
```
[14:20:31] upstream: 502 Bad Gateway from 10.2.4.12
[14:20:35] upstream: 504 Gateway Timeout to green-instance-17
```

carol_prod: feature-flag for new routing logic is on. toggling kill-switch for `canary-edge-split` now.

alice_oncall: toggled flag -> `canary-edge-split=false` :thumbsup:

ben_sre: traffic weight back to blue in control plane, but DNS TTL 120s means some flows still hit green. we need mitigation for sticky clients: 1) set regional abort route for green to return 503 quickly 2) remove heavy work from green instances 3) open support comms.

carol_prod: applying abort route to green instances now (`egress-route: abort-503`)

deploy-bot: abort-route applied to green pool in eu-west.

ben_sre: monitoring error rate — dropped from 12% -> 2% over last 3 minutes. latency still a bit elevated for affected clients.

alice_oncall: customer-impact note: affected subset = EU customers behind certain ISP CDNs honoring long DNS caching. approx 3% of global traffic, concentrated in EU. CS notified and drafting proactive message.

carol_prod: we also pushed a fast rollback of the model binary on green to reduce resource drain.

ben_sre: can we accelerate DNS propagation? TTL still in cache for some ISPs; engineering ops reached out to CDN partners for cache flush requests.

alice_oncall: handoff to ben for containment and root cause. I will open incident channel + postmortem template.

ben_sre: ack. I'll keep this incident open and run postmortem once stable. collecting logs and canary metrics. next steps: reproduce stale-DNS scenario in staging, add stronger kill-switch path that flips routing at edge, reduce default TTL for future rollouts.

incident-bot: Incident updated to SEV2 -> SEV1? No, remains SEV2. Pager sound cleared at 14:46UTC.

alice_oncall: closing live pager loop for now — monitoring for 30m. assigning owner @ben_sre to write RCA.

ben_sre: noted. creating ticket INF-2024-912 and assigning to eng-runtime + networking for follow-ups.

carol_prod: thanks all. quick retrospective: control-plane flip was correct but network cache behavior and a missing edge-level kill path caused customer-visible errors. will include in postmortem. :memo:
